diagnosis: Left ureteral stone (6 mm), treated with ureteroscopy and laser lithotripsy. A temporary left ureteral stent was placed.
hospital_course: You came to the emergency department with severe left flank pain and nausea. A CT scan showed a 6 mm stone in the left ureter. On {procedure_date} you had ureteroscopy. The stone was broken up and removed, and a stent was placed. Your pain is now controlled with oral medicine and you are eating and drinking normally.

medications.name: Tamsulosin
medications.note: This relaxes the ureter and eases stent discomfort.

medications.name: Ibuprofen
medications.frequency: every 8 hours as needed for pain
medications.note: Take with food. This is available over the counter.

diet: You should drink enough fluids to make at least 2.5 liters of urine a day. For most people this means about 3 liters (12 cups) of fluid daily, mostly water.
Please avoid high-oxalate foods such as nuts, spinach, and rhubarb.
You should limit sodium to less than 2,300 mg per day.
Do not cut back on calcium from food.
activity: You may walk and do light activity right away.
No heavy lifting over 10 pounds until your stent is removed.
care: You may shower; no baths or swimming while the stent is in place.
It is normal to have some pink urine, urgency, or mild flank discomfort while the stent is in place.
monitoring: Strain all of your urine through the strainer provided and save any stone pieces in the container. Bring them to your follow-up visit.
Check your temperature every evening for 7 days.

follow_up.purpose: a discussion of a 24-hour urine test

warning_signs: a fever of 101 F (38.3 C) or higher with chills
severe pain that your medicine does not control
chest pain, trouble breathing, or fainting
call_clinic: you see heavy bleeding or clots
